data_literals:
Our own forced aligner (no external tools): transcript -> CMUdict phones -> left-to-right chain of phone substates with
optional silence between words -> Viterbi over Module 2's state scores. Output = phone segments like the LibriSpeech alignments.
Used to label his non-test recordings; his 10 test clips are never aligned or used for calibration.

Top-only readouts at equal bytes: shared vs private nonlinear correction (EXPLORATION). Written 18 Nov 2026 ~20:1x by the agent (reviewer 5.5).
Source: review council 18 Nov (all 3: "decisive next control is a byte-matched top-only shared head") + reviewer Q8 test 2 (add private narrowed to the
shared width = containment at equal width). Checks in council_2026-11-18/COUNCIL_CHECK.md, Q7_Q8_CHECK.md.
All arms: base6 trunk w 232, linear skip Linear(w, 55) + a separate linear blank Linear(w, 1) (S's blank parameterisation, so blank paths match),
one nonlinear bank h1 = Linear(w, U) reading ONLY the trunk top g, GELU, h2 = Linear(U, 54) writing the 54 nonblank outputs (blank stays linear, as S).
Heads exist for the auxiliary teaching loss only (same AUXW as S and G) and are dropped at export (subclass of ArmG, as G).
  TS  shared:  h2 dense. U fitted to S's exported bytes.
  TP  private: h2 block-diagonal, output k reads only its own group (np.array_split of U over 54). U fitted to S's bytes.
  TN  private narrowed to TS's U (fewer bytes; equal width and inputs: the containment comparison).
Init: nn.Linear default, except the surviving h2 weights of TP/TN are redrawn for their TRUE fan-in (uniform +-1/sqrt(group size)), so the private
branch is not ~sqrt(54) quieter at the start (reviewer Q2 / council: spec2 started 7.35x small).
Known answers (selftest): TS has zero structural zeros; TP/TN masks block-diagonal with every output >= 1 unit; TS / TP bytes within 0.5 % of S;
a TP forward with an off-block h1 unit perturbed leaves every other output's logit unchanged.
Usage: python3 -I base6sy.py <TS|TP|TN> <tag> <seed> <epochs>; base6sy.py bytes (writes logs_base6/base6sy_budget_<A>.json).

exp142 black box: 80 log-mel -> conv (stride 2) -> BiGRU -> 39 phones + blank, CTC, greedy decode (DESIGN_exp142.md).
Same audio, labels and refs as the kept system: fit/cal = phones.split() files with ph_{fit,cal}.npz labels; eval sets = realcut_*.npz
files + segs labels (the exact refs phones46.run_set scores, phones46.py:28). Scorer = p44.edit, PER = sum edits / sum ref length.
Usage: bb142.py feats                                   (build the log-mel caches)
       bb142.py train SHAPE LR SEED EVALSETS [EPOCHS]  (SHAPE wide2 | narrow3; EVALSETS comma list, first = early-stop set)
Env: SHUF=1 shuffles label sequences across training utterances (broken control); PARAMS overrides the budget.
RECIPE=b0 (exp143): standard extras = SpecAugment (2 freq masks <= 15 of 80, 2 time masks <= min(40, 10 % of length)), AdamW wd 1e-2,
average of the 3 best libriA checkpoints (kept only if it is not worse on the early-stop set).
CTX=k (exp144, node P2): the model sees each TRUE segment alone plus k frames each side (k=0: no cross-segment context); outputs are
taken only for the segment's own frames and concatenated per utterance, CTC on the utterance. Uses true cuts at test time too. fp32 only.

Arm 2c labels (ARM_2c_DESIGN_2026-11-15.md section 3): variant token sequences (spec 4d: 39 phonemes -> 53 tokens + SIL) and
per-frame phone labels for the split heads, for the 5.4 h training pool (fit + cal, the base5 utterance order).
Variants are set by RULES FROM CONTEXT on the MFA alignment (phones with stress digits + word tier); the audio is not inspected.
Hard check: every variant sequence, with SIL removed and each token mapped back to its 39-phone spelling, must equal the base5 label
sequence of the same utterance exactly (base5_{fit,cal}.npz y_i). Any mismatch aborts.
Frame labels: ph_{fit,cal}.npz 'ph' (39 = silence, -1 = unknown) cut to base5 frame counts (diff <= 3 frames; missing tail = -1).
Writes cache/v2c_{fit,cal}.npz: y0..y{n-1} (variant ids, int16), n, f (frame labels, int8, concatenated), flens.
Usage: python3 labels2c.py [selftest]

Phase 0b / 0e / 0f input (docs/PLAN.md section 2): rescore saved checkpoints on clean / hard / his voice, CPU, inference only.
Per (model, set): greedy PER with sub / del / ins, hyp/ref, per-utterance (edits, ref phones, sub, del, ins) for the speaker bootstrap (0g).
Log-probabilities (float16) are cached for the first seed of each family (0e beam, 0f deletion positions) under CACHE/phase0_lp/.
Resumable: one JSON line per (model, set) in logs_base5/phase0_score.jsonl; done pairs are skipped.
Order: cleanS + him for every model first (new information), then the hard sets.
EXPLORATION. cleanS is TRAINING-speaker data for base100 (the 100 h model).
Usage: python3 phase0_score.py   (nice 19, 2 threads)

Module 2: 22 articulatory-feature detectors (closed-form shrunk Gaussians on masked inputs + Platt) and the
phone-state composer (LDA on the 22 clipped log-odds: w = S^-1 mu, the decorrelated GLS of DESIGN v2).
Data: LibriSpeech dev-clean (30 speakers fit detectors, 10 speakers calibrate + fit composer), test-clean (40 unseen speakers) test.
Pass marks fixed BEFORE results (DESIGN v2, reviewer's estimates):
  2. detector AUROC mean >= 0.85, none < 0.75 (test-clean)
  3. oracle-segmented phone accuracy top-1 >= 65 %, top-3 >= 86 % (test-clean)
Usage: python phones.py build | fit | eval
Step 5a: his 10 clips, dictionary labels timed by our aligner, current hybrid r76 model (LibriSpeech cal only). NIGHT_REPORT step 5.

Robustness test: the current best phoneme module (SEGALL = detectors + 108 measurements + 40 mel, segmental LDA; and SEG108
control), calibrated exactly as before (dev-clean only), run ONCE on LibriSpeech test-other (harder speakers / recordings).
Compare to test-clean: SEGALL 61.4 / 87.7, SEG108 57.4 / 85.2.

GPU cap gate v2 (Part C v6.5; review round 5 C5.7). Replaces gpu_gate.py for every GPU job. The cap comes from the APPROVAL record, the
commitments from the APPROVED LEDGER, never from the caller.

Files (default in this folder):
  approved.json   {cap_h, option, ledger_path, ledger_sha256, reserve_frac}  written when the author approves; ABSENT = every job refused.
  gpu_spend.jsonl events {ev: "hist"|"begin"|"charge", job, gpu_h?, t?, interrupted?}; ABSENT = refused. Seeded with the historical spend.
Rule for job J (a row key of the approved ledger, scope inside the approved option):
  need = spent(all charges) + allowance(J) + (1 + reserve_frac) * sum(expected_gpu_h of every approved row not yet charged, J excluded)
  need <= cap_h, else refused. allowance(J) = the row's worst_gpu_h (the job runs under that hard timeout).
Refused also: ledger file digest != approved; J not an approved row / out of scope; J already charged; any job begun and not charged
(one GPU job at a time; run `recover` first); a caller cannot pass cap, allowance or commitments (no such arguments exist).
`run J -- cmd ...` = check, begin, run cmd under `timeout allowance`, charge exactly once (interrupted if rc != 0 or timeout).
`recover` charges every begun-but-uncharged job at min(allowance, now - begin) as INTERRUPTED; interrupted jobs are never scoring-eligible
(`eligible J` returns False). Runners must launch GPU work only through `run` (audit: grep the runner for 'gpu_gate2.py run').
no approval record (approved.json): every GPU job refused

Controlled reader for SEALED panels: REGISTER / BIND / RELEASE (MASTER_PLAN Part C v6.5 C9 2). Fail closed everywhere.

REGISTER (before a comparison's first run): register(reg_name, protocol_path) writes locks/<reg_name>.register.json with the protocol sha256
  and appends it to locks/REGISTRY.jsonl. Refused if any panel the protocol names already has an access record (every comparison that will
  use a panel must be registered before that panel's first release). Protocol fields used here: arms, seeds, panels[{name, set_file,
  set_sha256, items[{utt, speaker, t}], release_path}]. (sec2_q2c_entry.py reads the same protocol and the release records.)
BIND (after training): bind(reg_name, slots) with slots = {arm: {seed: pt_path}}: exactly the protocol's arms x seeds; each checkpoint and
  its run json are hashed; the run must be complete (len(log) == epochs, no stop_after) and its GPU job eligible (gpu_gate2.eligible) unless
  the slot is listed in the protocol's 'legacy_slots' (old runs from before the gate; recorded as such). Written once (O_EXCL).
RELEASE (once per panel): release(panel) finds every registration naming the panel; each must be bound. It creates the ACCESS record
  locks/<panel>.access.json with O_EXCL BEFORE any model reads the set (a second or concurrent release fails there); then scores every
  bound slot, each in a FRESH python process whose recipe environment (RIGHT, NORM, FEAT, WARP, RWIRE_SEED) is set from the run's own
  config before import, using the training script's own evaluate(..., items=True) (parity by construction); the child re-hashes the
  checkpoint and asserts RIGHT, NORM, budget and frozen-tree string equal the run config. Rows {panel, arm, seed, utt, speaker, e, t, h}
  are checked against the protocol items (same utts, speakers, reference counts) and written once per registration; then the release
  record (panel, items_sha256 = sec2_q2c_entry.items_digest, rows sha256, bind sha256) is written once. A crash after the access record
  and before the release record leaves the panel COMPROMISED: release refuses forever; the owner decides (no silent retry).
Recipes the child cannot reproduce exactly are REFUSED: FEAT != '' (feature copies), WARP != '' (needs the panel's own warp estimates,
  realization 134; adapter TO DO for Q4), NORM fixed (statistics not in the checkpoint).
Usage: python -I reader_v65.py selftest | parity <tag> <set> | register <name> <protocol> | bind <name> <slots.json> | release <panel>

Locked scorer for SEALED test sets (MASTER_PLAN Part C v6.3 C2.0; review round 3 C2.0 / C5.4). The ONLY code path that reads a sealed set.
Training scripts (base6.py / base6s.py) score validation sets only (EVALSETS allowlist) and cannot load sealed files: the sealed caches live in
cache/sealed/, outside the path base5_next.load() reads.

Protocol (all asserted, fail closed):
1. A LOCK file step0/locks/<question>.lock.json is written BEFORE any sealed access (make_lock): question id, the comparison (arm -> list of
   model .pt paths with sha256 and their run json), the sealed set name + sha256 of its cache file, the statistic, and the lock's own sha256
   recorded in step0/locks/LOCKS.txt (append-only). A lock cannot be rewritten (exists -> refuse).
2. score <lock>: re-hash every model and the set; any mismatch -> refuse. Every model of the lock is scored in one call (no partial opening);
   a (lock, model sha) pair already in step0/locks/SCORED.jsonl -> refuse (one locked pass per model and set).
3. Output: per-utterance edits e, reference length t, hypothesis length h, utterance id; totals; written next to the lock as
   <question>.scores.json (exists -> refuse). Scoring runs on the CPU in float32 with the same decode as the training script's evaluate().
Models: base6 plain (config without 'arm', NORM must be causal: fixed-norm statistics are not saved in the .pt) and base6s arms (make(arm, bud)).
Usage: python -I score_locked.py selftest | lock <spec.json> | score <question>      (CPU venv with torch; no GPU).

Self-scored warp (18 Nov, reviewer; EXPLORATION after 2-I / 2aW_): the same unsupervised VTLN rule as vtln_grid.py (per utterance and alpha in
GRID: mean negative entropy of the model's output on the warped input; alpha = argmax of the summed scores of the speaker's OTHER utterances),
but the SCORER is base6 itself (default e60_r12_causal_s0, plain), not the stage-1a base5 model: on the phone no second model would be needed.
Writes cache/vtln_S_{set}.npz (alpha, scores, grid, spk; spk copied from vtln_{set}.npz). Known answer: the scores of the stage-1a scorer
re-computed here for 20 libriA utts with this code path equal vtln_libriA.npz scores (atol 1e-3), so the only change is the scorer.
GPU (python3, python -I, under the GPU lock). Usage: RIGHT=12 NORM=causal python -I vtln_self.py
known answer: old scorer via this path, max |diff| vs vtln_libriA.npz

Warp alphas for train-clean-100 (19 Nov, reviewer; plan step a: warp + noise recipe at 2 MB / 100 h). CALIBRATION.
Same rule and scorer as vtln_grid.py / WARP=W (stage-1a base5 0.66 MB s0; mean negative entropy per alpha on GRID 0.80-1.20 step 0.04;
speaker alpha = argmax of the summed scores), run on the GPU batched over the grid (vtln_self.py path, known answer below).
One deviation, for cost: only PER_SPK utterances per speaker (seeded) are scored at each speed; a scored utterance gets the leave-one-out
alpha of its speaker's other scored utterances (as vtln_grid), an unscored one the argmax of all scored ones. Writes cache/vtln_tc100{,_sp0.9,_sp1.1}.npz
(alpha, scores of the scored rows, scored, spk, grid). Known answer: this path reproduces vtln_libriA.npz scores on 20 utts (atol 1e-3).
Usage: RIGHT=12 python3 -I vtln_tc100.py [sets...]   env PER_SPK (default 20), LIMIT (score only the first N speakers: smoke)
